standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the vanishing of the pullback of the class to the algebraic closure, both in degree above one and, in degree one, the identification of the group with the corresponding group over the residue field.

core_obligations: Degree above one (proof lines 17375-17383): for q > 1 the class xi dies after pulling back to the algebraic closure by the vanishing theorem, and the lemma on directed colimits lets one choose a finite extension K'/K over which it already dies, so one may take k' = k and Z = X.

Reduce to constant finite coefficients (proof lines 17385-17396): for q = 1 the coefficient sheaf corresponds to a discrete Galois module M which is the union of its finite stable subgroups, so one reduces to a finite abelian group annihilated by n; after a finite extension of K the action of the Galois group on M may be assumed trivial, and one may replace M by a direct summand, hence by Z/dZ with d dividing n.

Build the cover over the algebraic closure (proof lines 17398-17422): the class pulls back to an element of H^1(X_{residue}, Z/dZ) = H^1(X_{closure}, Z/dZ) which classifies a Z/dZ-torsor, giving a finite etale T -> X over the algebraic closure with a transitive Z/dZ-action on the fibre over the rational point; a connected component T' of T is a finite etale Galois cover with group G a subgroup of Z/dZ whose order divides a power of n, and xi maps to zero on T' by the defining property of T.

Descend and conclude (proof lines 17424-17442): a limit argument descends T' -> X to a finite etale Galois cover Z -> X_{k'} with group G over a finite extension k' of k; after enlarging k' one may assume Z splits over the rational point, and since the image of xi in H^1(Z over the closure, Z/dZ) is zero, the directed colimit lemma produces a finite subextension K'/K containing k' over which xi dies.
proof_roadmap: Dispose of the degrees above one by the vanishing theorem and a limit argument.
Reduce the degree one case to constant coefficients Z/dZ with Galois action made trivial by a finite extension.
Realize the class by a torsor, pass to a Galois connected component, and descend the resulting cover to a finite extension of the base field.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for an extension of fields K/k, a smooth affine curve X over k with a rational point, and a torsion coefficient sheaf on Spec(K) with order invertible in k, every class in degree q > 0 dies after a finite extension K'/K and a finite etale Galois cover Z -> X_{k'} of group order dividing a power of n that splits over the rational point (statement lines 17356-17373). The proof (proof lines 17375-17443) treats the degrees above one by the vanishing theorem and a limit argument, and the degree one case by reducing to constant coefficients, realizing the class by a torsor, taking a Galois connected component and descending it. H2: a multi-step reduction with five independent inputs, written out in full.
